answer.body:
This is a screening rank of expansion opportunity under the momentum_heavy scenario for East North Central census-division airports that clear the model's enplanement gate. It is not a financial valuation.

Chicago O'Hare International (ORD) has the highest calculated score at {F351}. Dane County Regional Truax Field (MSN) is next at {F352}. MSN is not flagged as tied with ORD. Appleton International (ATW) at {F353} is flagged as tied with MSN. Indianapolis International (IND) at {F354} is not flagged as tied with ATW. John Glenn Columbus International (CMH) at {F355} is not flagged as tied with IND. Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County (DTW) at {F356} is flagged as tied with CMH. Ford International (GRR) at {F359} is flagged as tied with MDW. Cleveland Hopkins International (CLE) at {F360} is flagged as tied with GRR. General Mitchell International (MKE) at {F361} is not flagged as tied with CLE. James M. Cox Dayton International (DAY) at {F362} is not flagged as tied with MKE. A tie flag does not mean those scores are equal; each score is its own calculated finding.

Each score combines an unconstrained FAA forecast of enplanement change, realized passenger growth, and home-CBSA per-capita income. The forecast term is an FAA forecast, not observed traffic and not unmet demand. Realized growth and income are calculated. The forecast comparison for every scored airport is the same fiscal-year window as ORD ({F264.period}). Realized growth uses the same passenger window as ORD ({F300.period}). Income uses the same period as ORD ({F313.period}).

For ORD, the forecast enplanement change is {F264}, realized passenger growth is {F300}, and home-CBSA per-capita income is {F313}.

For MSN, the forecast enplanement change is {F262}, realized passenger growth is {F298}, and home-CBSA per-capita income is {F312}.
